messages:
maria: Heads up — I'm prototyping a tiny console panel that shows per-route marginal token cost and the contribution from cache savings. Trying to figure out what we compute server-side vs in the UI. Thoughts?

owen: Love the idea. key question: do we show 'effective token cost' (after cache amortization) or raw model/token cost + cache delta? both are useful but mixing can confuse billing. :thinking:

maria: Agreed. My current thinking: server returns raw token_cost, cache_savings, and precomputed amortized_cost so clients can display either. We already emit token_count per-invocation in telemetry.

jia: If we precompute amortized_cost server-side we need a stable amortization window and sampling rules. otherwise numbers will jump as we retroactively assign saved tokens.

sam: +1 on predictable windows. Also we should avoid double-counting shared prefetch savings across routes. had that bug in the prefetched credits prototype.

maria: Good call. Proposal: amortize prefetch/cache savings per billing window (24h) and emit a field in the invocation stream: "cache_credit_fraction" and "amortized_cache_savings_per_invocation". Then console can roll up per-route.

owen: Can we stick to existing telemetry schema? adding two fields is OK but let's be explicit in the spec. Example SQL to compute a rollup if we need to run ad-hoc: ```SELECT route, sum(token_count) AS tokens, sum(model_cost_tokens) AS raw_cost, sum(amortized_cache_savings_per_invocation) AS cache_savings, (sum(model_cost_tokens)-sum(amortized_cache_savings_per_invocation))/sum(token_count) AS effective_per_token FROM invocations WHERE ts >= '2024-11-01' GROUP BY route;```

jia: That SQL is fine for analytics, but for the live panel we need an API that returns pre-aggregated numbers per-route with sampling info. otherwise latency and cardinality bite us.

maria: Exactly. Plan: ingest adds the two fields (cache_credit_fraction, amortized_cache_savings_per_invocation). An aggregation job computes daily per-route pre-aggregates and a realtime micro-agg for last-hour. API returns both. UI shows: raw, amortized, and per-token effective.

sam: UX nit: show confidence / sampling rate and a little tooltip explaining amortization window + how shared prefetch is split. customers asked about 'why did my metric change' a lot. :eyes:

maria: We'll add a small 'explain' modal that links to rollout docs and an example calculation. Also gate on a feature flag so enterprise customers can opt into precomputed amortization vs raw only.

owen: One more internal API question — should the backend expose both per-invocation amortized value and the aggregate only? storing per-invocation amortized numerically will bloat our events. maybe emit amortization_credit_bucket (enum) + sample_weight and compute actual dollars at aggregation?

jia: I prefer numeric amortized value per invocation if we can afford it. It simplifies analytics, debugging and helps audits. But if size is a concern, bucket + weight works. We should benchmark event size delta.

maria: I'll run a quick bench on event payload increase and storage. if <5% we keep numeric. otherwise bucketed.

ops-bot: Deploy preview: feature flag "cost-panel-amortization" created for orgs: beta_redwood, test-ops. Docs: https://confluence/reports/amortization-spec :white_check_mark:

sam: For rollout, start with internal orgs + small beta customers, then expand after 2 weeks of stability and a short audit. Also add an alert if amortized_savings spikes >50% day-over-day for a route.

maria: Thanks — I'll update the spec and push a PR for the telemetry schema. pinging @owen for API review when PR is ready.

owen: happy to review. please include example responses for the UI (last-hour + daily aggregates) and the sampling/confidence fields.

maria: Will do. TL;DR: server will emit raw token/model cost + amortized cache savings per-invocation (or bucketed if size is an issue), aggregation jobs produce per-route pre-aggregates, UI shows raw vs effective cost and explains amortization. Rollout behind flag.

sam: Sounds good. small follow-up: can the panel have an optional 'what-if' slider to toggle different amortization windows (1h/24h/7d) and see impact? would be super helpful for PMs.

maria: Love that. we'll add it to the backlog as a v1 enhancement. thanks everyone.
